home.subtitle: When the Tonle Sap turns and the full moon rises, Cambodia gathers by the river for three nights of light, boat races and thanksgiving.

intro.title: A celebration of water, moon and harvest
body: At the end of the rainy season the Tonle Sap river reverses its flow, moving back toward the great lake. This natural event marks a time of abundance and has been welcomed for generations.

Bon Om Touk brings that welcome to the riverbanks: illuminated boats, the sound of racing drums, moon salutation and the sharing of ok ambok. It is both a public celebration and a quiet expression of gratitude.

about.title: The river that changes direction
about.lead: Bon Om Touk is Cambodia's Water Festival, held at the end of the rainy season when the Tonle Sap river reverses and flows back toward the Tonle Sap lake.

river.title: A remarkable natural cycle
body: During the monsoon, the Mekong pushes water into the Tonle Sap river, which flows northwest into the lake. When the rains ease, the Mekong level falls and the river reverses, draining the lake southeast toward Phnom Penh.
This reversal brings fish and replenishes the fields. The festival celebrates the water, the harvest and the full moon that lights the nights.

history.title: Meaning and memory
body: The festival is widely understood as a thanksgiving for the river's bounty and a celebration of the new fishing and rice season.
Boat races recall the importance of the river and, in Khmer tradition, historic naval victories. The observance is also a time for families to gather and make merit.

traditions.title: What visitors can see
body: Racing boats with painted eyes and drums move along the river; small illuminated boats and lanterns are set afloat after dark; people salute the full moon; and ok ambok — flattened rice with coconut and banana — is shared.
Programmes differ from place to place and from year to year. Always check current local announcements before making travel plans.

pp_riverside.name: Sisowath Quay Riverside
pp_riverside.desc: The long riverfront promenade in central Phnom Penh, facing the Mekong and the Tonle Sap. It is a natural meeting point for evening strolls and festival lights.
highlights: Wide pedestrian walkway along the water
Views of the river and passing boats
Easy access to cafés and the old centre
pp_riverside.bestTime: Early evening, before the crowds grow.
pp_riverside.gettingThere: Located in central Phnom Penh; reachable by taxi, tuk-tuk or a walk from the nearby streets.

pp_royal_palace.name: Royal Palace
pp_royal_palace.desc: The royal compound in central Phnom Penh, known for its traditional Khmer architecture and the nearby Silver Pagoda. It stands a short distance from the riverfront.
pp_royal_palace.bestTime: Earlier in the day when the light is soft.
pp_royal_palace.gettingThere: In central Phnom Penh, a short walk or tuk-tuk ride from Sisowath Quay.

pp_wat_phnom.name: Wat Phnom
pp_wat_phnom.desc: A hilltop temple in Phnom Penh, associated with the city's founding story. The surrounding park offers a calm pause above the busy streets.
highlights: A short ride from the riverfront
pp_wat_phnom.gettingThere: In the centre of Phnom Penh; taxi or tuk-tuk is the easiest option.

pp_independence_monument.name: Independence Monument
pp_independence_monument.desc: A landmark in central Phnom Penh commemorating independence, set at a roundabout near the river and the main boulevards.
highlights: Near the riverfront and Norodom Boulevard
pp_independence_monument.bestTime: Evening, when the area is lit up.
pp_independence_monument.gettingThere: A short tuk-tuk or taxi ride from Sisowath Quay.

pp_koh_pich.name: Koh Pich (Diamond Island)
pp_koh_pich.desc: A river island district south of central Phnom Penh with modern buildings, a broad waterfront and easy access to the river.
pp_koh_pich.gettingThere: South of the centre; take a taxi or tuk-tuk across the bridge.

sr_angkor_wat.name: Angkor Wat
sr_angkor_wat.desc: The great temple complex near Siem Reap, famous for its Khmer architecture and its reflection in the surrounding moat at sunrise.
sr_angkor_wat.gettingThere: A short drive from Siem Reap town by tuk-tuk or car.

sr_pub_street.name: Pub Street
sr_pub_street.desc: The busy central street in Siem Reap, lined with restaurants, cafés and small shops. It is a lively place to eat after an evening by the river.
sr_pub_street.gettingThere: In the centre of Siem Reap, walkable from most nearby hotels.

sr_river.name: Siem Reap River
sr_river.desc: The small river running through Siem Reap, with bridges and promenades close to the old centre. Local festival announcements often mention this area.
sr_river.gettingThere: In central Siem Reap; walk or take a short tuk-tuk ride.

sr_floating_villages.name: Tonle Sap Floating Villages
sr_floating_villages.desc: Communities on the Tonle Sap lake whose homes and daily life follow the changing water level. Visits are usually arranged as boat trips from the Siem Reap area.
highlights: Life on Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake
Views of stilted and floating homes
sr_floating_villages.gettingThere: Usually reached by road and then boat through a local operator.

kp_riverside.name: Kampot Riverside Promenade
kp_riverside.desc: A relaxed waterfront along the Kampot River, with views of the violet hills and small boats. The promenade is simple and easy to explore on foot.
kp_riverside.gettingThere: In central Kampot; walk from the town centre or take a tuk-tuk.

kp_durian_roundabout.name: Durian Roundabout
kp_durian_roundabout.desc: A central Kampot landmark marked by a large durian sculpture. It is a well-known meeting point and a playful symbol of the province's famous fruit.
kp_durian_roundabout.gettingThere: In the centre of Kampot town, reachable on foot.

kp_bokor.name: Bokor Mountain
kp_bokor.desc: A mountain ridge above Kampot with cool air, mist and panoramic views. The area includes old hill-station buildings and a large temple on the plateau.
highlights: Cooler air than the town below
kp_bokor.bestTime: Morning, when views are often clearer.
kp_bokor.gettingThere: Reached by road from Kampot; transport should be arranged locally.

kp_hand_bridge.name: Riverside Hand Viewing Bridge
kp_hand_bridge.desc: A distinctive riverside viewpoint near Kampot, shaped like an open hand. It is a popular spot for photos over the water and the hills beyond.
kp_hand_bridge.gettingThere: A short tuk-tuk or taxi ride from central Kampot.

more_kep.name: Kep
more_kep.desc: A small coastal town near Kampot known for its seafood, quiet beaches and views across to Phu Quoc island.
more_kep.bestTime: Daytime for the coast, evening for dinner.
more_kep.gettingThere: Reached by road from Kampot or Phnom Penh.

more_battambang.name: Battambang
more_battambang.desc: A laid-back city in northwest Cambodia, known for old French-era buildings, pagodas and a slow riverside atmosphere.
more_battambang.gettingThere: Reached by road or domestic flight from Phnom Penh.

more_kampong_cham.name: Kampong Cham
more_kampong_cham.desc: A provincial town on the Mekong, a convenient stop for seeing the river away from the capital and crossing to the nearby island.
more_kampong_cham.gettingThere: Reached by road from Phnom Penh.

more_kratie.name: Kratie
more_kratie.desc: A town on the Mekong in northeastern Cambodia, known as a place to see Irrawaddy dolphins in the river.
more_kratie.bestTime: Early morning or late afternoon for dolphin watching.
more_kratie.gettingThere: Reached by road from Phnom Penh or Kampong Cham.

more_sihanoukville.name: Sihanoukville
more_sihanoukville.desc: A coastal city in southern Cambodia with beaches and harbours, a different setting from the river festivals inland.
more_sihanoukville.gettingThere: Reached by road or domestic flight from Phnom Penh.

ok_ambok.name: Ok Ambok
ok_ambok.detail: Flattened rice is pounded and mixed with coconut and banana. It is shared with family and neighbours during the festival nights.

boat_racing.name: Boat Racing
boat_racing.detail: Long racing boats with painted eyes compete to the sound of drums. Races are held in several provinces, with programmes announced locally.

floating_lanterns.name: Floating Lanterns
floating_lanterns.detail: Small illuminated boats and lanterns are set afloat after dark, filling the river with moving light.

moon_salutation.name: Moon Salutation
moon_salutation.detail: People gather by the water to salute the full moon, a moment of respect and thanksgiving at the heart of the festival.

tips.title: Practical travel tips
tips.subtitle: Simple, general advice to help you enjoy the festival safely and respectfully.
tips.note: Conditions and official guidance can change. Check current local information before you travel.

transport.title: Getting around
items: Plan extra time: roads and bridges near river events can be busy.
Taxis and ride-hailing are common in cities; agree the price before setting off where needed.
Keep your accommodation address saved in Khmer or on a map.

crowds.title: Crowds and valuables
items: The full moon night is usually the busiest; arrive early for a good viewing spot.
Keep phones, wallets and bags close, especially in dense crowds.
Agree a meeting point with companions in case you are separated.

waterSafety.title: Boat and water safety
items: Wear a life jacket on boats and never step onto unstable floating platforms.
Choose licensed boat operators and avoid trips in strong wind or heavy rain.
Do not swim in festival traffic areas; keep a close watch on children near the water.

etiquette.title: Pagoda etiquette
items: Dress modestly: cover shoulders and knees when entering a pagoda or temple.
Remove shoes before entering temple buildings and speak softly.
Ask before photographing monks or people at prayer.

food.title: Food and ok ambok
items: Ok ambok is flattened rice mixed with coconut and banana; it is a festival favourite.
Try local snacks from busy stalls where food turns over quickly.
Drink bottled or filtered water if your stomach is sensitive to changes.

weatherSafety.title: Weather and health
items: Late November is generally dry and warm, but evenings by the river can be cool.
Carry sun protection in the day and a light layer for the night.
Bring basic medicine and check that your travel insurance covers your plans.

scams.title: Scam awareness
items: Be cautious of inflated prices for transport, tours or priority viewing spots.
Check the fare or price before accepting a ride or booking a trip.
Keep copies of important documents and use ATMs in well-lit, busy places.
